title: A conducting slab on a hot plate radiating through a transparent fluid to its surroundings (lattice conjugate heat transfer)
source: Steady one-dimensional conduction through series thermal resistances with a radiating surface between them: the top cell's balance (T₀ − T_c)/R₁ = (T_c − T₁)/R₂ + ε σ (T_c⁴ − T_sur⁴) (F. P. Incropera, D. P. DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, §3.1, the thermal circuit, and §1.3.1, the surface energy balance), with R₁ and R₂ the lattice's resistances from the hot plate to the slab's top cell and from it through the fluid to the cold plate; T_c solved by bisection to round-off

quantities.quantity: temperature of the slab's top cell (y = 0.21875)
quantities.reason: the lattice's discrete steady state is the series-resistance balance exactly (README), reached to round-off by the end of the run; 8 and 16 cells both match to 10⁻⁹ K

quantities.quantity: power the slab radiates, ε σ (T_c⁴ − T_sur⁴) over the column's cross-section Δx²
quantities.reason: the same balance; the radiated power is 52 % of what the hot plate supplies
